note: This skill exists to be the single owner of normative thresholds. Cases 1-4 check that it produces the right number with the right version; 5-7 check the claims that most sources get wrong (APCA, 1.4.12's direction, automated scores); 8 is a near miss that must route to ref-sp-ux-design.

evals.prompt: Is 16px grey text at #767676 on a white background compliant?
evals.expected_output: Contrast measured against the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text, with the large-text carve-out explained and the WCAG version stated.
assertions: Applies 4.5:1 for normal text and names SC 1.4.3
States that large text (>=18pt, or >=14pt bold) uses 3:1 and that 16px does not qualify
States the WCAG version (2.2) rather than an unversioned 'WCAG'

evals.prompt: Our icon buttons are 20x20 pixels with 4px between them. Is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: Fails SC 2.5.8 (24x24 AA) unless the spacing exception applies; the spacing exception is evaluated.
assertions: Names SC 2.5.8 and the 24x24 CSS px minimum
Evaluates the spacing exception (24px-diameter circles must not intersect) rather than answering with the size alone
Distinguishes the AAA 44x44 figure from the AA requirement

evals.prompt: A sticky header covers the focused element when I tab up the page. Which criterion is that?
evals.expected_output: SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), Level AA, with the 'entirely hidden' wording and the AAA variant distinguished.
assertions: Names SC 2.4.11 at Level AA
States the AA bar is 'not entirely hidden' and that 2.4.12 (AAA) requires no part hidden
Identifies sticky headers/banners as the common failure

evals.prompt: What zoom and viewport widths should we test at?
evals.expected_output: 320 CSS px for reflow (1.4.10) and 200% text resize (1.4.4), with the relationship to 400% zoom on 1280px explained.
assertions: Gives 320 CSS px for SC 1.4.10 and 200% for SC 1.4.4
Explains that 320px corresponds to 1280px at 400% zoom
Distinguishes page zoom from text-only zoom

evals.prompt: We're switching our contrast checks to APCA since it's the WCAG 3 algorithm.
evals.expected_output: Correction: APCA was removed from the WCAG 3 draft in July 2023, WCAG 3's contrast algorithm is undetermined, WCAG 3 is not expected before ~2030; conform to WCAG 2.2 and treat APCA as supplementary.
assertions: States that APCA was pulled from the WCAG 3 working draft in July 2023
States that the WCAG 3 contrast algorithm is 'yet to be determined'
Recommends conforming to WCAG 2.2 contrast
Allows APCA as a supplementary check without calling it a standard
Corrects the premise directly rather than hedging

evals.prompt: WCAG requires 1.5 line height, so I've set line-height: 1.5 everywhere. Done?
evals.expected_output: Correction: SC 1.4.12 is a resilience requirement about user-imposed spacing, not a mandate to ship 1.5; the real test is that nothing breaks when the user applies the values.
assertions: Corrects the direction of SC 1.4.12
Lists the four user-imposed values (1.5 line height, 2x paragraph, 0.12x letter, 0.16x word)
Names fixed-height containers as the typical failure
Does not endorse the original premise

evals.prompt: Lighthouse gives us 100 on accessibility. Can we say the product is accessible?
evals.expected_output: No. Automated tools cover a minority of barriers; report as 'no automated violations' and name the manual passes still required.
assertions: States that a clean automated run is a floor, not a pass
Names things automation cannot judge (alt meaningfulness, focus order logic, custom widget behaviour)
Recommends the keyboard, zoom, spacing-override, and screen-reader passes
Does not recommend an accessibility overlay

evals.prompt: How should I structure the spacing scale for our design system?
evals.expected_output: Routes to ref-sp-ux-design; spacing scale construction is not an accessibility threshold question.
assertions: Routes to ref-sp-ux-design
Does not invent an accessibility justification for a spacing scale
